issues_detected.description: keywords lists only four terms: 'health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'. The rubric bar for searchability is five or more keywords covering domain, methods and conditions; terms the record itself uses prominently (speech, audiomics, acoustic biomarkers, machine learning, neurological disorders, respiratory disorders) are absent from the keyword list.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add keywords for speech, audiomics, acoustic biomarkers, machine learning and the disease cohorts represented.

issues_detected.description: The record sets id and doi to the version-independent DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 while declaring version: 3.1.0, and the citation resolves to the version-specific DOI https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66. version_access.latest_version_doi holds the 3.1.0 DOI even though its own source_caveats states that 'Every PhysioNet release page in the bundle labels 10.13026/37yb-1t42 as the DOI of the latest version'. The choice is documented and both DOIs are PhysioNet-registered, but a versioned record carrying the unversioned DOI in its doi slot is a semantic mismatch a machine consumer would not detect.
issues_detected.recommendation: Use the version-specific DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 in doi for a record whose version is 3.1.0, and put the version-independent DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 in latest_version_doi, or state explicitly that the record describes the dataset across versions.

issues_detected.description: version_access.version_details states 'There is no erratum; a changelog for each dataset version is published online', while errata records two entries (release 2.0.1 authorship corrections; release 3.1.0 fixes to broken Parquet files and back-filled diagnosis data). The errata source_caveats explains that the two statements come from the project documentation and the PhysioNet release notes respectively, so the conflict is documented rather than hidden.
issues_detected.recommendation: Drop the 'no erratum' sentence from version_details or qualify it as the project documentation's claim.

issues_detected.description: content_warnings asserts 'The dataset includes the transcription of free speech tasks', while participant_privacy, preprocessing_strategies and known_limitations all state that free-speech transcripts were removed before release. The content_warnings source_caveats resolves this by noting the PhysioNet pages rank higher and that 'the transcription of free speech is not present in the current registered-access release', but the warning text itself is left as stated by the stale healthsheet.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reword the first content warning to describe what the current release actually contains, keeping the caveat about the healthsheet.

issues_detected.description: subpopulations lists 'pediatric voice and speech disorders' as one of the five disease cohort categories, but the record's referent is the adult dataset ('contains data for 833 adult participants'), and the pediatric cohort is 'carried in related_datasets rather than merged in'. The identification text describes the program's cohort design rather than the released data's subpopulations.
issues_detected.recommendation: State that four of the five program cohorts are represented in the adult release and that the pediatric cohort is released separately.

issues_detected.description: external_resources contains the entry 'AI-readiness for Biomedical Data - Bridge2AI Recommendations' as a bare title in a list that otherwise carries URLs and DOIs, so it does not resolve.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the URL or DOI for the Bridge2AI AI-readiness recommendations, or move the title into the description field.

issues_detected.description: variables documents only the four linking keys (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames); no feature-level or phenotype-level variables are listed, and is_tabular is absent. Column semantics are delegated to the shipped JSON data dictionaries described in file_collections. Adequate for integration but thin for a dataset with nine feature files and eighteen diagnosis tables.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the principal feature variables (with units and ranges, e.g. torchaudio pitch 80-500 Hz, sparc pitch 50-550 Hz, which the record already states in preprocessing_strategies) and set is_tabular.

issues_detected.description: ethical_reviews documents the USF single IRB with its thirteen-version revision history, the Canadian research ethics boards and the separate genomic protocol, but contains no conflict-of-interest disclosure. The only conflict-adjacent statement is in funders: 'The National Institutes of Health had no role in the preparation, review or approval of the audiomics viewpoint'.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a conflicts-of-interest statement (or an explicit 'none declared') to ethical_reviews.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes gives 'a period of 12 months' plus IRB phase milestones and its source_caveats states 'No start or end date for collection of the released data is stated in the bundle'. version_access lists per-version DOIs for 1.0, 1.1, 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 but none for 2.0.0 and 2.0.1. issues_detected.recommendation: Source calendar collection dates and the 2.0.x DOIs from PhysioNet if resolvable.

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts states 'No analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted.' This documents a governance gap honestly; participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is nonetheless explicitly assessed ('does not achieve k-anonymization at k greater than or equal to two'), so the privacy-logic expectation is satisfied.
issues_detected.recommendation: None for the datasheet; reference a DPIA if one is conducted for a future release.

semantic_insights: Scope check passed: the pediatric dataset is expressed as a typed related_datasets entry (is_supplemented_by, target https://doi.org/10.13026/mf9s-5r03, version DOI 10.13026/h995-bt35) and the record-level source_caveats states 'the pediatric dataset is carried in related_datasets rather than merged in'. The pediatric Synapse URL (syn73617068) appears only inside that related_datasets description; the only Synapse URL in distribution_formats and raw_sources (syn72370534) is the adult raw-audio route.

DOI hygiene is strong: 10.13026/37yb-1t42, 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, 10.13026/249v-w155, 10.13026/k81f-qr68, 10.13026/mf9s-5r03 and 10.13026/h995-bt35 all carry the PhysioNet registrar prefix; 10.57764/qb6h-em84 (Health Data Nexus), 10.5281/zenodo.12760724 and zenodo.14148755 and zenodo.13834653 (Zenodo) and 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926 (ISCA) are plausible registrar prefixes.
RRID:SCR_007345 in the citation is format-valid and correctly attributed to PhysioNet, exactly as PhysioNet's recommended citation prescribes.

Grant numbers OT2OD032720 (core), 3OT2OD032720-01S1 (supplement cited on PhysioNet) and 1OT2OD032720-01 (feasibility publication) all match the NIH pattern; the funders source_caveats refuses to record two visibly corrupted renderings ('3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1', 'Award #3Tf-OTOD03272001S2') rather than normalizing them. PhysioNet's own grants U24EB037545 and R01EB030362 are NIH-pattern-valid and correctly attributed to the platform under maintainers.

Cross-field ethics logic is consistent: involves_human_subjects: true is backed by the USF single IRB with Canadian REB separation, four consent modalities with the teach-back comprehension check ('potential participants are asked to explain what they have understood'), HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect-identifier and sensitive-element removal with an itemized identifiers_removed list, and an explicit re-identification risk statement that semantically justifies withholding raw audio to controlled access.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true is consistent with the enrolled cohorts (human_subject_research.special_populations names 'Participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias'), and special_protections describes the comprehension check applied to them; this resolves the boolean inconsistency present in earlier VOICE records.

Temporal ordering is coherent: the IRB protocol runs from 17 January 2023 (v1) to 11 July 2025 (v13); releases run 1.0 (end of November 2024) through 3.1.0 (2026-05-01); issued: '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z' matches the 3.1.0 release date; and updates.source_caveats lists the five observed PhysioNet release dates against the stated semi-annual cadence.

Known biases use the standard taxonomy (selection_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias) with affected_subsets and mitigation strategies; the measurement_bias entry ('Participants were screened for different disorders based on site, so they also had their data collected with different devices') is a substantive confounding observation.

Source-conflict handling is systematic: per-field source_caveats reconcile the Rudzicz/Rudzizc and Siu/Sui spellings, the 10,000-vs-30,000 enrollment targets, the 61,937-item figure that 'is not a count of audio recordings but of derived items', the healthsheet's 'No' on cleaning against the documented audit protocol, and the DTUA's not-HIPAA-covered classification against the applied HIPAA de-identification.

The record correctly separates historical parameters from current ones: 'Release 1.1 computed spectrograms with a 512-point FFT and no time-domain downsampling ... The parameters stated above are those of releases 3.0.0 and 3.1.0.'

strengths: Referent discipline: the record declares its referent (the adult dataset, release 3.1.0 on PhysioNet) in a record-level source_caveats, keeps the pediatric dataset strictly in related_datasets with its own DOIs and Synapse route, and confines historical release 1.1 parameters to explicitly labelled caveats.

Identifier and funding correctness: every DOI carries a plausible registrar prefix, the RRID is valid and correctly attributed to PhysioNet, and the three NIH award renderings are pattern-valid and attributed to their sources, with two corrupted strings explicitly refused.

Ethics documentation is complete and internally consistent: single IRB with Canadian REB separation, multi-modality consent with a comprehension check, HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect-identifier removal with an itemized list, a candid k-anonymity statement, and an at-risk boolean that matches the enrolled dementia and psychiatric cohorts.

Reproducibility-grade processing detail: STFT window/hop/FFT parameters, mel-bin count, per-feature frame rates, pitch ranges, the generating toolkit version (b2aiprep 3.0.0), the audit protocol with its ten-per-cent monthly QC sampling, and per-feature record counts.

Systematic source-conflict handling: name spellings, affiliations, enrollment targets, the derived-item count, the healthsheet's cleaning answer and the DTUA's HIPAA classification are each reconciled on the object concerned with the ranking rule stated.
weaknesses: Only four keywords, below the searchability bar and omitting speech, audiomics, machine learning and the represented conditions.

The doi slot carries the version-independent DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 for a record declaring version 3.1.0, while the citation and latest_version_doi carry the 3.1.0 DOI; documented, but inverted relative to PhysioNet's own 'latest version' labelling.
variables lists only the four linking keys and is_tabular is absent; feature-level variables whose parameters the record already states elsewhere are not enumerated.

Two stale-source statements are left in the primary text and corrected only in caveats: 'The dataset includes the transcription of free speech tasks' in content_warnings and 'There is no erratum' in version_access.
No conflict-of-interest disclosure, no calendar collection dates, no DOIs for releases 2.0.0 and 2.0.1, and one external_resources entry that is a title rather than a URL.
recommendations: Expand keywords to at least eight terms covering speech, audiomics, acoustic biomarkers, machine learning and the four adult disorder families.
Put the version-specific DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 in doi and the version-independent DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 in latest_version_doi, matching PhysioNet's labelling.
Enumerate the principal feature variables (torchaudio pitch 80-500 Hz, sparc pitch 50-550 Hz, 60 MFCCs, 40-category posteriorgrams) in variables and set is_tabular.
Reword the free-speech content warning and the 'no erratum' sentence to describe the current release, retaining the caveats about the source conflict.
Add a conflicts-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews, a URL for the AI-readiness recommendations, and the 2.0.x version DOIs if resolvable.

scope_check.detail: Checked per the source_manifest scope declaration for VOICE. The pediatric release appears in related_datasets (is_supplemented_by, target https://doi.org/10.13026/mf9s-5r03, version DOI 10.13026/h995-bt35) with its own participant counts, REB and Synapse route (syn73617068), and the record-level source_caveats states it 'is carried in related_datasets rather than merged in'. Its identifiers do not appear in file_collections, distribution_formats or raw_sources; the only Synapse URL in distribution (syn72370534) is the adult raw-audio route. Descriptive pediatric mentions in human_subject_research.special_populations, at_risk_populations and creators (Jennifer Siu, 'Lead investigator at the pediatric site') are labelled as the separate cohort. One mild bleed is noted: subpopulations lists 'pediatric voice and speech disorders' among the five cohort categories without stating that it is absent from the adult release.
